claims.text: UN News (5 June 2026), citing IOM: "nearly 1.5 million people without a stable place to live"; "more than 18,000 people" displaced in May 2026 alone from Cité Soleil attacks; the number of internally displaced people in Port-au-Prince rose "above 300,000" for the first time on record; "more than 110,000 Haitians" have been forcibly returned to the country since the beginning of 2026. IOM Chief of Mission Gregoire Goodstein: "Haiti's displacement crisis is entering an even more alarming phase."

UN News (19 July 2026): "1.47 million people have fled their homes largely due to violence." During a Cité Soleil violence outbreak, "at least 542 people were killed and 355 injured," and "at least 176 women and girls were raped." Separately, at least 87 deaths have been reported from vigilante killings of suspected gang collaborators. "Around 6.4 million people need humanitarian assistance" and "more than 5.8 million people are expected to go hungry this year."

UN News (20 July 2026), 'LIVE: Haiti endures violence and hunger, but hopes grow for a more secure future': reconfirms IOM's nearly-1.5-million displacement figure (originally reported 5 June 2026) as still current, reports on a UN Security Council discussion of the Gang Suppression Force, and notes that Haitian security forces have begun recording limited successes against armed gangs, pushing some criminal groups out of strategic locations in Port-au-Prince and reopening some major roads; the article provides no updated death-toll or displacement aggregate beyond the figures already reported. Re-checked 5 August 2026: no newer UN News, ReliefWeb, or OCHA report supersedes the 19-20 July 2026 figures (1.47M displaced, 542 killed in the Cité Soleil outbreak, 6.4M in humanitarian need, 5.8M facing hunger).

Re-confirmed by direct fetch on 6 August 2026: IOM's Haiti Situation Report (May 2026 DTM round, published 22 June 2026) remains the source of the national 1.47 million displacement figure; a newer IOM Emergency Tracking Tool update (ETT 103, posted 5 August 2026) covers only one municipality (Saint-Michel de l'Attalaye, Artibonite) and does not supersede the national aggregate.

Re-checked 7 August 2026 via direct fetch of reliefweb.int/country/hti: no newer national displacement or casualty aggregate has been published beyond the 19-20 July 2026 figures (1.47 million displaced nationwide, 542 killed in the Cite Soleil violence outbreak); the most recent items are a localized 31 July 2026 Emergency Tracking Tool bulletin on displacement in Saint-Michel de l'Attalaye, Artibonite (a municipal, not national, figure) and a 14 July 2026 UN Secretary-General report, neither of which revises the national totals.

New localized report found 8 August 2026: a BINUH (UN Integrated Office in Haiti) report posted to ReliefWeb 6 August 2026 states that, in the Plaine du Cul-de-Sac area and Cite Soleil specifically, "between 6 March and 31 July 2026, at least 613 people were killed and 375 others injured, primarily during confrontations between criminal gangs... more than 176 women and girls were subjected to rape, including gang rape" and "more than 18,000 people [were] forced to flee their homes" in that area; it also documents an attack after a 13 June FIFA World Cup match that killed at least 61 people. This is a more specific, localized casualty count for a sub-national area and period, and does not supersede the nationwide IOM displacement total (1.47 million) or the broader 19 July UN News Cite Soleil figure (542 killed) already cited, which cover different scopes; no newer nationwide displacement aggregate has been published.

OCHA's Latin America & the Caribbean Weekly Situation Update (7 August 2026) reports that armed violence in Saint-Michel de l'Attalaye, Artibonite department, displaced approximately 4,216 people on 28 July, with three displacement sites forced to close, triggering additional secondary displacement — a new localized incident that does not supersede the nationwide IOM displacement total (1.47 million) already on file.

description: Escalating gang violence across Haiti, concentrated in and around Port-au-Prince, has driven internal displacement to record levels through mid-2026. IOM figures cited by UN News put the total at nearly 1.5 million people without a stable place to live as of 5 June 2026, after a surge of more than 18,000 people displaced from Cité Soleil in May 2026 alone pushed the number of internally displaced people in Port-au-Prince above 300,000 for the first time on record; more than 110,000 Haitians have also been forcibly returned to the country since the start of 2026, compounding the crisis. A subsequent UN News report (19 July 2026) put total displacement at 1.47 million and detailed a Cité Soleil violence outbreak earlier in 2026 in which at least 542 people were killed, 355 injured, and at least 176 women and girls raped, with residents fleeing to neighbouring Drouillard; the same report cites roughly 6.4 million people in need of humanitarian assistance and more than 5.8 million expected to face hunger this year. A further UN News report (20 July 2026) reconfirms the nearly-1.5-million displacement figure amid a Security Council discussion of the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force, with some initial, limited security gains reported in parts of Port-au-Prince. No authoritative source has declared the crisis contained or resolved, and no newer displacement or death-toll aggregate has been published as of 5 August 2026. New localized report found 8 August 2026: a BINUH (UN Integrated Office in Haiti) report posted to ReliefWeb 6 August 2026 states that, in the Plaine du Cul-de-Sac area and Cite Soleil specifically, "between 6 March and 31 July 2026, at least 613 people were killed and 375 others injured, primarily during confrontations between criminal gangs... more than 176 women and girls were subjected to rape, including gang rape" and "more than 18,000 people [were] forced to flee their homes" in that area; it also documents an attack after a 13 June FIFA World Cup match that killed at least 61 people. This is a more specific, localized casualty count for a sub-national area and period, and does not supersede the nationwide IOM displacement total (1.47 million) or the broader 19 July UN News Cite Soleil figure (542 killed) already cited, which cover different scopes; no newer nationwide displacement aggregate has been published. Re-checked 9 August 2026: OCHA's Latin America & the Caribbean Weekly Situation Update (7 August 2026) reports a new localized incident — armed violence in Saint-Michel de l'Attalaye, Artibonite department, displaced approximately 4,216 people on 28 July, forcing the closure of three displacement sites — which does not supersede the nationwide IOM displacement total (1.47 million) or the 19 July UN News Cité Soleil toll (542 killed) already on file.
